title: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs
body:
Read the chapter → [Exodus 10](/bible/exodus/10)

## Introduction

This reading covers [Exodus 10](/bible/exodus/10) through 13: the plagues of locusts and darkness, the death of the firstborn announced and executed, the institution of the Lord's Passover and the feast of unleavened bread, Israel thrust out of Egypt after 430 years, the sanctifying of the firstborn, and the pillar of cloud and fire leading the people. The session opens with a precursor from [Proverbs 21](/bible/proverbs/21) and Romans 9: the things that were written aforetime were written for our learning, and the Most High is in absolute control of the kings of the earth.

**[Exodus 10:1](/bible/exodus/10#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/exodus/10#v1)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh: for I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants, that I might shew these my signs before him:

- The Most High hardened the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants so that he might show his signs and exemplify his power in the earth. After he brought down Egypt and delivered the people, every nation feared Israel and the God of Israel.
- The king's heart is in the hand of the Lord; he turns it whithersoever he will. He is in control of the mind of the kings of the world, so there is no need to worry over who becomes president or who gets put in office; either way the Most High is in control.
- The scripture said to Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might show my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth. He has mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth.
- The potter has power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour and another unto dishonour. Some nations are honourable, which are the Israelites, and some are dishonourable; Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated. The vessels of wrath were fitted to destruction, endured with much longsuffering so the Most High could show how powerful he is; that is why Esau had to be set on such a high level, so that when he brings these people down all will know God is truly all powerful.
- The same holds in spiritual Egypt today: the Most High will harden the hearts of the rulers of this kingdom so they will not let Israel go and will continue to oppress, because in the affliction the people will seek him early. It does not matter who is voted into office; whoever sits in the seat, the Most High turns him about like the rivers of water.
- The things that were written aforetime were written for our learning, and the thing that hath been is that which shall be. That is why so many similarities appear between the captivities: this captivity carries the marks of Egypt, of Babylon, and of the Greeks, because these things must come to pass.

  Precepts:
  - **[Proverbs 21:1](/bible/proverbs/21#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/proverbs/21#v1)</sup> The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.

    The king's heart is in the hand of the Lord; he turns rulers whithersoever he will, no matter who is voted in.
  - **[Romans 9:15-18](/bible/romans/9#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/romans/9#v15)</sup> For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.
    >
    > <sup>[16](/bible/romans/9#v16)</sup> So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.
    >
    > <sup>[17](/bible/romans/9#v17)</sup> For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.
    >
    > <sup>[18](/bible/romans/9#v18)</sup> Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth.

    He has mercy on whom he will have mercy; Pharaoh was raised up for this same purpose, that the Most High might show his power in him.
  - **[Romans 9:19-22](/bible/romans/9#v19)**
    > <sup>[19](/bible/romans/9#v19)</sup> Thou wilt say then unto me, Why doth he yet find fault? For who hath resisted his will?
    >
    > <sup>[20](/bible/romans/9#v20)</sup> Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?
    >
    > <sup>[21](/bible/romans/9#v21)</sup> Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?
    >
    > <sup>[22](/bible/romans/9#v22)</sup> What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction:

    The potter has power over the clay to make one vessel unto honour and another unto dishonour; the vessels of wrath were fitted to destruction.
  - **[Romans 9:13](/bible/romans/9#v13)**
    > <sup>[13](/bible/romans/9#v13)</sup> As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.

    Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated; Jacob is the honourable vessel and Esau the dishonourable.
  - **[Romans 15:4](/bible/romans/15#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/romans/15#v4)</sup> For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

    The things written aforetime were written for our learning; the history of Egypt teaches this captivity.
  - **[Ecclesiastes 1:9](/bible/ecclesiastes/1#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/ecclesiastes/1#v9)</sup> The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.

    The thing that hath been is that which shall be; the captivities repeat their patterns.
  - **[Hosea 5:15](/bible/hosea/5#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/hosea/5#v15)</sup> I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.

    In their affliction they will seek me early; the oppression is used to wake the people up.

**[Exodus 10:2](/bible/exodus/10#v2)**

> <sup>[2](/bible/exodus/10#v2)</sup> And that thou mayest tell in the ears of thy son, and of thy son’s son, what things I have wrought in Egypt, and my signs which I have done among them; that ye may know how that I am the Lord.

- The fathers are to tell in the ears of their sons and their sons' sons what things the Most High wrought in Egypt. That is what Israel does every year at the Passover, giving honour to the things he did in Egypt and the way he delivered the people out of the hand of the oppressors.
- The same deliverance will be told again: it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt, but, The Lord liveth that brought them up from the land of the north, out of Babylon the Great where the people sit today.

  Precepts:
  - **[Jeremiah 16:14-15](/bible/jeremiah/16#v14)**
    > <sup>[14](/bible/jeremiah/16#v14)</sup> Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt;
    >
    > <sup>[15](/bible/jeremiah/16#v15)</sup> But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north, and from all the lands whither he had driven them: and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.

    No more Blessed be the Lord that brought Israel out of Egypt, but out of the land of the north; the greater exodus is still ahead.

**[Exodus 10:3-6](/bible/exodus/10#v3)**

> <sup>[3](/bible/exodus/10#v3)</sup> And Moses and Aaron came in unto Pharaoh, and said unto him, Thus saith the Lord God of the Hebrews, How long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself before me? let my people go, that they may serve me.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/exodus/10#v4)</sup> Else, if thou refuse to let my people go, behold, to morrow will I bring the locusts into thy coast:
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/exodus/10#v5)</sup> And they shall cover the face of the earth, that one cannot be able to see the earth: and they shall eat the residue of that which is escaped, which remaineth unto you from the hail, and shall eat every tree which groweth for you out of the field:
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/exodus/10#v6)</sup> And they shall fill thy houses, and the houses of all thy servants, and the houses of all the Egyptians; which neither thy fathers, nor thy fathers’ fathers have seen, since the day that they were upon the earth unto this day. And he turned himself, and went out from Pharaoh.

- Moses went in to Pharaoh with a staff and an ultimatum: how long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself? Let my people go, or tomorrow, in twenty four hours, the locusts come into thy coast.
- The locusts would cover the face of the earth so no one could see the ground, eat the residue that escaped the hail, and fill the houses of Pharaoh, of his servants, and of all the Egyptians, such as neither their fathers nor their fathers' fathers had seen.

**[Exodus 10:7-11](/bible/exodus/10#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/exodus/10#v7)</sup> And Pharaoh’s servants said unto him, How long shall this man be a snare unto us? let the men go, that they may serve the Lord their God: knowest thou not yet that Egypt is destroyed?
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/exodus/10#v8)</sup> And Moses and Aaron were brought again unto Pharaoh: and he said unto them, Go, serve the Lord your God: but who are they that shall go?
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/exodus/10#v9)</sup> And Moses said, We will go with our young and with our old, with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds will we go; for we must hold a feast unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/exodus/10#v10)</sup> And he said unto them, Let the Lord be so with you, as I will let you go, and your little ones: look to it; for evil is before you.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/exodus/10#v11)</sup> Not so: go now ye that are men, and serve the Lord; for that ye did desire. And they were driven out from Pharaoh’s presence.

- Pharaoh's own servants pleaded with him: how long shall this man be a snare unto us? Knowest thou not yet that Egypt is destroyed?
- Moses answered that all would go, young and old, sons and daughters, flocks and herds, for we must hold a feast unto the Lord. The Most High loves to see Israel gathered together in unity; that is why so many feast days bring the nation together to honour him.
- Pharaoh offered to let only the men go, and Moses and Aaron were driven out from his presence.

  Precepts:
  - **[Psalm 133:1](/bible/psalms/133#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/psalms/133#v1)</sup> Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!

    Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity; the feasts gather the nation.

**[Exodus 10:12-15](/bible/exodus/10#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/exodus/10#v12)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up upon the land of Egypt, and eat every herb of the land, even all that the hail hath left.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/exodus/10#v13)</sup> And Moses stretched forth his rod over the land of Egypt, and the Lord brought an east wind upon the land all that day, and all that night; and when it was morning, the east wind brought the locusts.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/exodus/10#v14)</sup> And the locusts went up over all the land of Egypt, and rested in all the coasts of Egypt: very grievous were they; before them there were no such locusts as they, neither after them shall be such.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/exodus/10#v15)</sup> For they covered the face of the whole earth, so that the land was darkened; and they did eat every herb of the land, and all the fruit of the trees which the hail had left: and there remained not any green thing in the trees, or in the herbs of the field, through all the land of Egypt.

- The hail with fire wrapped in it had already destroyed much; now the locusts came on an east wind to clear out the remaining crops, even all that the hail had left.
- The locusts covered the face of the whole earth so that the land was darkened; there were so many that they blocked out the sun. They ate every herb and all the fruit of the trees, and there remained not any green thing in all the land of Egypt.

**[Exodus 10:16-17](/bible/exodus/10#v16)**

> <sup>[16](/bible/exodus/10#v16)</sup> Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste; and he said, I have sinned against the Lord your God, and against you.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/exodus/10#v17)</sup> Now therefore forgive, I pray thee, my sin only this once, and intreat the Lord your God, that he may take away from me this death only.

- When the judgment got real, Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste and confessed, I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you. Everything had been eaten by the locusts, and now he begged that this death only be taken from him.

**[Exodus 10:18-20](/bible/exodus/10#v18)**

> <sup>[18](/bible/exodus/10#v18)</sup> And he went out from Pharaoh, and intreated the Lord.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/exodus/10#v19)</sup> And the Lord turned a mighty strong west wind, which took away the locusts, and cast them into the Red sea; there remained not one locust in all the coasts of Egypt.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/exodus/10#v20)</sup> But the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, so that he would not let the children of Israel go.

- Moses entreated the Lord, and a mighty strong west wind took away the locusts and cast them into the Red Sea; there remained not one locust in all the coasts of Egypt.
- But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, so that he would not let the children of Israel go. The Most High is in ultimate control even of the devil; he is the omnipotent master of all existence, and nothing can be done outside his will.

**[Exodus 10:21-23](/bible/exodus/10#v21)**

> <sup>[21](/bible/exodus/10#v21)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/exodus/10#v22)</sup> And Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven; and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days:
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/exodus/10#v23)</sup> They saw not one another, neither rose any from his place for three days: but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.

- Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven, and there was thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days, even darkness which may be felt. They saw not one another, neither rose any from his place.
- But all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings; the Most High put a difference between his people and the Egyptians.

**[Exodus 10:24-26](/bible/exodus/10#v24)**

> <sup>[24](/bible/exodus/10#v24)</sup> And Pharaoh called unto Moses, and said, Go ye, serve the Lord; only let your flocks and your herds be stayed: let your little ones also go with you.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/exodus/10#v25)</sup> And Moses said, Thou must give us also sacrifices and burnt offerings, that we may sacrifice unto the Lord our God.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/exodus/10#v26)</sup> Our cattle also shall go with us; there shall not an hoof be left behind; for thereof must we take to serve the Lord our God; and we know not with what we must serve the Lord, until we come thither.

- After three days of darkness Pharaoh called for Moses: go, serve the Lord, only let your flocks and your herds be stayed. Go, but leave all your possessions in Egypt.
- Moses refused: our cattle also shall go with us, there shall not an hoof be left behind. Not a hoof, a hair, or a heifer would stay in Egypt, for thereof must Israel take to serve the Lord, and we know not with what we must serve the Lord until we come thither.

**[Exodus 10:27-29](/bible/exodus/10#v27)**

> <sup>[27](/bible/exodus/10#v27)</sup> But the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let them go.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/exodus/10#v28)</sup> And Pharaoh said unto him, Get thee from me, take heed to thyself, see my face no more; for in that day thou seest my face thou shalt die.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/exodus/10#v29)</sup> And Moses said, Thou hast spoken well, I will see thy face again no more.

- The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart yet again, and Pharaoh threatened Moses: see my face no more, for in that day thou seest my face thou shalt die. After the rivers turned to blood, the hail with flaming fire, the locusts, and the darkness, Pharaoh still thought he was in a position to give out threats. That is the deceivableness of the strong delusion: God sends it so that they should believe a lie.
- The same delusion falls on Israel when the people go reprobate in their sins: believing the Sabbath begins when the sun comes up, that anything can be eaten on Passover, or that the leaven to be put away is only the heart. Sin blinds.
- Moses answered, Thou hast spoken well, I will see thy face again no more.

  Precepts:
  - **[2 Thessalonians 2:11](/bible/2-thessalonians/2#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/2-thessalonians/2#v11)</sup> And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie:

    God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie; Pharaoh was deceived into thinking he could threaten the servant of God.
